record.paper_title: Imaging with LINC-NIRVANA, the Fizeau interferometer of the Large Binocular Telescope: state of the art and open problems
record.original_question: How can LINC-NIRVANA image reconstruction recover high-dynamic-range astronomical scenes in which bright point sources are superimposed on diffuse faint structure, such as a bright star lying on top of a diffuse cloud in young stellar object observations? Existing adaptive regularization handles separated bright and faint components only when there is a large brightness difference and angular separation, so the unresolved case is reconstruction when the bright source and diffuse emission overlap.

evidence.quote: bright star over a diffuse cloud

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Fizeau interferometric imaging system that produces multiple long-exposure images $g_j$, $j=1,\dots,p$, of the same astronomical scene at different parallactic angles, each modeled as

$$g_j = K_j f + b_j + n_j,$$

where $f \ge 0$ is the unknown sky brightness distribution defined on a discrete pixel grid, $K_j$ is a known linear shift-invariant imaging operator (convolution with the corresponding point spread function of the interferometric baseline at orientation $j$), $b_j$ is a known background, and $n_j$ is Poisson photon noise. Assume the target $f$ has the form

$$f = c\,\delta_{x_0} + h,$$

i.e.\ the superposition of one (or several) bright point sources of unknown intensity $c>0$ located at known positions $x_0$ and a non-negative diffuse component $h \ge 0$ representing extended faint structure, such that the integrated flux ratio between the point source and the diffuse component is very large (high dynamic range) and the angular support of $h$ contains $x_0$ (the bright source overlaps spatially with the diffuse emission rather than being well separated from it).

Design a reconstruction algorithm — for instance a regularized maximum-likelihood method of the form

$$\min_{c \ge 0,\, h \ge 0}\; \sum_{j=1}^p D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\big(g_j \,\|\, K_j(c\,\delta_{x_0}+h)+b_j\big) + \mu\, R(h),$$

with $D_{\mathrm{KL}}$ the Kullback–Leibler (Csiszár) divergence appropriate for Poisson data and $R$ a smoothness-promoting regularizer acting on the diffuse component — that, in the overlapping high-dynamic-range regime, simultaneously recovers (i) the intensity $c$ of the bright point source and (ii) the diffuse structure $h$ underneath it, without the point source's reconstruction artifacts contaminating the recovered diffuse emission. Establish convergence and stability properties of the resulting iterative scheme, and prove (or characterize) the conditions on the dynamic range, on the point spread functions $\{K_j\}$, and on the regularization functional $R$ under which the diffuse component beneath the bright source can be faithfully recovered.
artifact.category_tag: Inverse problems in astronomical image reconstruction
artifact.status_search_result: Follow-up work has developed split-component reconstruction methods that model the target as a bright point source plus a diffuse component, with a smoothness-enforcing regularizer on the diffuse part and Poisson likelihood. Simulations on stellar jets have shown success in some regimes, but the fully overlapping case in which the bright source sits inside (rather than next to) the diffuse emission remains only partially addressed — methods exist as heuristics validated on simulations, without general theoretical guarantees on dynamic-range limits and recovery fidelity.

status_evidence.title: Image reconstruction for observations with a high dynamic range: LINC-NIRVANA simulations of a stellar jet
status_evidence.snippet: The image to be reconstructed is the sum of two terms: one for the star (position assumed known) and one for the jet; a smoothness regularization is added to the Poisson log-likelihood.
status_evidence.claim: A split point-source-plus-diffuse Poisson reconstruction has been proposed and tested via simulations of a stellar jet.

status_evidence.title: Deconvolution of multiple images with high dynamic range and an application to LBT LINC-NIRVANA
status_evidence.snippet: Deconvolution method for multiple high-dynamic-range images applied to LINC-NIRVANA.
status_evidence.claim: Prior algorithmic work addresses high-dynamic-range multi-image deconvolution for this instrument, but the fully overlapping case remained an open issue.

status_evidence.title: Advances in the reconstruction of LBT LINC-NIRVANA images
status_evidence.snippet: Adaptive regularization techniques for LINC-NIRVANA reconstruction.
status_evidence.claim: Adaptive regularization handles separated bright and faint components but the unresolved overlapping case was identified as not yet solved.
